rated_messages.input_message: What can you do right now to break the automatic habit of smoking to help you feel better? Pause. Close your eyes. And take 10 slow breaths.
It's normal to have some doubts during a quit attempt. Keep your quit reasons on hand to remind yourself if ever you feel uncertain or undecided.
Think of your anxious mind like a toddler throwing a tantrum. The best way to respond is to quietly watch, but not give in.
When you are stressed, it is easy to focus on the things that are going wrong. Take a few moments to focus on 5 things that have gone well or that you are thankful for this week.
If you find yourself with a few minutes to spare, it can be nice to read back over old messages. It's also a chance to reply to ones that you might have forgotten about!
Just because letting an urge pass isn't easy, doesn't mean that you can't do it. Try it, you might surprise yourself.
Try to avoid seeing other people smoke. It might sound basic but brain see, brain want! If you can, make life easier and avoid the people you used to smoke with for some time where possible.

Imagine that your urge is a backseat passenger trying to distract you from reaching your destination. See if you can choose to keep driving instead of allowing your urges to distract you from where you want to go.

Imagine walking into a social situation in three months' time as a non-smoker. Now hold that picture and imagine you're that person now. Seeing yourself as a non-smoker now can make it much easier to resist!

If you get any urges tonight, why not confront them head on? Ask the urge - what's it going to give you? It's not going to make you richer, or better looking, and it's not going to leave you if you give in either!
